repair.a: A header with an account ROOT (acc, acct, accnt, subacc) AND any word of ACCOUNT_ATTRIBUTE_WORDS never enters the backstop (_has_account_root and not _has_attribute_word). The whole-cell exclusions named the full words (Account Value); the abbreviated root takes the same exclusion keyed on the attribute word after it. Count headers (No. of Accounts) are unchanged.
repair.b: An 8-or-more digit run is identifier-like only when NO value in the same column (rows 2 and below) carries a number separator (NUMBER_SEPARATOR = [.,$%()'\s]). A hyphen and an underscore are identifier characters, so they are not separators. A column that mixes plain digit runs with decimals, commas, a dollar sign or a space is a money column. _identifier_like(value, money_column=False) keeps its one-argument form for the r19 definition test.

attribute_word_reasons: one reason per word in the ACCOUNT_ATTRIBUTE_WORDS dict in intake/template_reader.py, beside the constants
separator_interpretation: The order's 'another separator' is read as the number-formatting marks above (the decimal point, the thousands comma, the currency and percent signs, parentheses, an apostrophe, whitespace). This is the worker's reading, stated here for the L9 grader; a wider reading (any non-identifier character) would also be defensible and is not what was built.
